entries.title: How can a cocoon become a silk thread?
entries.answer: A silkworm spins a long strand around itself before it changes into a moth. Layers of that strand form the cocoon. For a kind of silk used in cloth, people gather cocoons and carefully unwind long threads from them. These can be joined into yarn that is often smooth and shiny. Silk fiber comes from a substance a caterpillar can make inside its body. Cotton fiber grows from a plant, so there are very different ways to get the threads that become fabric.
facts: The silkworm that supplies much textile silk is a moth caterpillar.

entries.title: How can a little hole make an image inside a dark room?
entries.answer: If a room is dark and there is a small hole in one wall, light from outdoors can enter and make an image on the wall across from the hole. Light travels in nearly straight lines through the air. Rays from high parts of the scene go downward after passing through the hole. Rays from low parts go upward. The scene appears upside down on the wall, even though everything outside stayed right side up.
facts: People call this setup a camera obscura, which means dark room.

entries.title: How can scissors cut with two moving edges?
entries.answer: Each half of a pair of scissors has a handle at one end and a blade at the other. Both halves turn around the same small pin. Closing the handles makes the sharp edges pass close beside each other. They push the paper in opposite directions along a short line, so it splits cleanly there. The point where the blades meet moves along as the handles close.
facts: On many scissors, using the part of the blade near the pin gives you more cutting force.

entries.title: How do kitchen tongs pinch food without touching it with your hands?
entries.answer: A common pair of kitchen tongs has two long arms joined at one end. The ends far from the join can grip a piece of food. Squeezing the handles brings those gripping ends together. When you loosen your hand, a spring can open the arms again. The long arms mean you can reach something in a pan while keeping your hand farther from the hot surface.
facts: Some tongs have rounded gripping ends, while others have ridges that help hold slippery food.

entries.title: How do tiny fibers become a sheet of paper?
entries.answer: Many kinds of paper start with tiny wood fibers. A mill separates the fibers and mixes them with water, making a wet mass called pulp. It spreads that pulp onto a moving screen. The water drains away while the fibers stay behind and catch on one another. Rollers press out more water, and the sheet dries. Old paper can sometimes be separated into fibers and used again. Shorter fibers or bits of ink can change how the recycled paper looks and feels.
facts: Pressing and drying remove water from a new sheet.

entries.title: How does a clothes dryer get water out of wet clothes?
entries.answer: A tumble dryer turns a big drum so wet clothes keep lifting and falling. This spreads them out and brings moving air to many parts of the cloth. Warm air helps liquid water in the fabric change into water vapor. Some dryers send the damp air outdoors through a vent. Other dryers collect the water inside the machine or send it down a drain.
facts: A dryer’s lint filter catches small bits of fiber that came loose from clothes.

entries.title: How does a dishwasher reach the dishes on both racks?
entries.answer: A dishwasher sends water through small holes in spray arms. The jets help spin the arms, sweeping water across the plates, bowls, and cups. Detergent helps lift food and grease while the spray carries them away. After washing, the machine drains the used water and sprays cleaner water to rinse the dishes. A big pan in the wrong spot can block an arm or shield a dish from the jets.
facts: Dishwasher racks have gaps so water can pass between the dishes.

entries.title: How does a toilet flush and fill again?
entries.answer: In many toilets, pressing the handle lets water rush from a tank into the bowl. The fast flow can fill a curved passage and start drawing water from the bowl down the drain. Air gets into the passage and stops that draw as the bowl empties. Fresh water then fills part of the bowl again. A valve lets water enter the tank until it reaches its usual level.
facts: The water left in the bowl helps keep air from the drain from moving into the room.

entries.title: How does an insulated bottle keep a drink warm or cold?
entries.answer: An insulated bottle often has two walls with very little air in the space between them. With so little air there, heat has a harder time moving through the gap. A lid also slows the movement of warm or cool air in and out of the bottle. If you put in a warm drink, it loses heat more slowly. A cold drink gains heat more slowly for the same reason.
facts: The word vacuum in vacuum bottle means a space with very little matter in it.

entries.title: How does soap help water wash away grease?
entries.answer: A greasy surface can make plain water form separate drops. Soap changes how these materials meet. Part of a soap molecule gets along with water, while another part gets along with oil. As the surface is rubbed or stirred, soap helps hold broken-up grease in small groups that the water can carry away. There is more to cleaning than making foam. A soapy mixture can carry away oil even where few bubbles are big enough for you to see.
facts: Soap can affect both water and oil because different parts of a soap molecule behave differently.

entries.title: What are the tiny threads in cloth made from?
entries.answer: A cloth can contain thousands of tiny strands called fibers. Some come from plants, like cotton and flax. Others come from animals, like wool from sheep or silk from certain insects. People can also make fibers from manufactured materials. Twisting many fibers together can make yarn. Weaving or knitting yarn can make a piece of fabric. Two shirts may feel different because of the kinds of fibers they use, the way those fibers were made into yarn, and how the yarn is joined.
facts: A fabric tag can tell you what fibers go into a garment.

entries.title: What does a number on plastic tell you?
entries.answer: Some containers have a small number surrounded by a three-sided shape. The number identifies a type of plastic material, which can help sorting. It does not by itself tell you where a container can be recycled. A local program might accept a bottle but have no way to handle an object made with some of the same material in another shape. Labels, food left inside, and mixtures of different parts can matter too. Local recycling rules give the most useful answer.
facts: The code identifies a general type of plastic resin.

entries.title: What happens inside a washing machine?
entries.answer: A washing machine helps water and detergent reach the dirt in fabric. In some machines a drum rolls the clothes over and over. In others a moving part in the middle swishes clothes through the water. The washer drains the dirty water and rinses the clothes with cleaner water. Near the end, it spins the clothes quickly to get out much of the water before drying.
facts: Some washers open at the front, while others open at the top.

entries.title: What happens to old glass bottles in recycling?
entries.answer: A glass bottle can sometimes become part of a new bottle. At a recycling plant the old glass may be sorted, cleaned and crushed into small pieces. The glassmaker can add those saved pieces to the ingredients melted for a new batch. Undesired pieces of pottery, a window pane or a baking dish can have different properties from bottle glass. That is why local collection rules can call for certain kinds of glass, even when all the objects look smooth or clear.
facts: Crushed glass ready to be used as an ingredient is called cullet.

entries.title: What part of a flax plant becomes linen?
entries.answer: A flax plant grows long groups of tough fibers inside its slender stems. After harvest, people loosen and remove other stem material so they can gather those fibers. The long strands can be twisted into yarn and woven into linen cloth. Linen and cotton both come from plants, but their fibers do not grow in the same place. A cotton plant makes its soft fibers around seeds. Flax fibers run along the stem and help give that stem support while the plant is alive.
facts: Linen fibers grow along the flax stem, not on the outside of a seed.

entries.title: Where does dirt go inside a vacuum cleaner?
entries.answer: A vacuum cleaner uses a fast fan to move air from the hose or floor head toward an outlet. Air in the room rushes into the opening and carries loose dirt with it. In some vacuums, a bag catches most of the dirt. In others, spinning air throws heavier bits into a bin. Filters help catch smaller bits before the air goes back into the room.
facts: Many vacuum cleaners use more than one kind of filter.

entries.title: Why can a rug make a room sound less echoey?
entries.answer: A hard floor reflects much of the sound that reaches it. A rug gives some of the moving air a tangle of fibers and small gaps to pass through. Some of the wave’s energy spreads into tiny motions and heat instead of coming back as another strong sound. Covering part of a hard surface can shorten the tail you hear after a clap.
facts: Soft curtains and padded seats can also absorb part of a room’s sound.

entries.title: Why can an onion make your eyes water?
entries.answer: A knife breaks many onion cells when it slices through their layers. Materials kept apart in an uncut onion can then mix. A few changes happen quickly, producing an onion substance that can travel through the air. If it reaches your eyes, it can irritate them, and your eyes make more tears to clear it away. An onion sitting whole has fewer open cells than a chopped one. That is why cutting the onion makes a bigger difference than simply placing it nearby.
facts: Cutting opens onion cells and lets substances inside meet.

entries.title: Why can salt melt ice on a road?
entries.answer: Ordinary water can freeze at a certain temperature, but water with dissolved salt in it can stay liquid below that temperature. Salt on an icy road can dissolve in small amounts of liquid water at the surface and form salty water. Under suitable conditions, that helps more ice melt into the liquid mixture. How much it works depends on the temperature and how much liquid is available. Salt can also damage plants or move into waterways, so many road crews use it carefully.
facts: Salt cannot melt road ice well in all temperatures.

entries.title: Why can soap make a bubble last?
entries.answer: A bubble forms when air stretches a thin liquid film around itself. Water alone usually cannot keep that delicate film from breaking for very long. Soap makes the film easier to stretch and helps it hold together longer. A floating bubble tends toward a round shape because its film pulls toward the smallest surface it can make around that amount of air. As water drains or evaporates from the film, weak spots can form, and the bubble may pop.
facts: A bubble contains air surrounded by a thin liquid film.

entries.title: Why do clothespins snap shut when you let go?
entries.answer: A common clothespin has two arms held together by a bent piece of springy wire. The part of the wire in the middle lets the arms turn a little. When you squeeze the back ends together, the front ends move apart. The spring is bent more than usual while you squeeze. When you let go, it pushes the front ends shut around the clothes and the line.
facts: A clothespin has two places to move: the ends you squeeze and the ends that hold the clothes.

entries.title: Why do some water drops leave white spots?
entries.answer: As rain or groundwater moves through rocks, it can pick up small amounts of minerals. Water with a lot of dissolved calcium or magnesium is called hard water. You usually cannot see those minerals floating in the water. When a drop dries on a faucet or glass, however, some mineral material can stay behind as a pale spot. The spot is a clue that the water was carrying something besides water molecules. Soap may also behave differently in hard water.
facts: Dissolved calcium or magnesium can make it harder for some soaps to make foam.

entries.title: Why does a breeze dry clothes on a line?
entries.answer: Water in a wet shirt can turn into water vapor and spread into the air. That change is called evaporation. Without much movement, the air close to the shirt can grow damp. A breeze carries some of that damp air away and brings other air to the fabric. A shirt spread out on a line also has more wet surface open to the air than one left in a heap.
facts: Drying may be slower when the air already holds a lot of water vapor.

entries.title: Why does a fan make you feel cooler?
entries.answer: A fan pushes air past your skin. The moving air can carry away heat when it is cooler than your skin. It also helps sweat dry faster. As sweat changes from liquid to vapor, it takes heat from your skin. In a closed room, a fan mainly moves the air already there. The breeze can make people feel cooler without lowering the room’s temperature.
facts: A fan can help moving air reach your skin even on a still day.

entries.title: Why does a longer wrench handle make turning easier?
entries.answer: A wrench grabs the sides of a nut so it can turn it. If you push near the far end of a long handle, your push has more turning effect than the same push close to the nut. Your hand also has to travel farther for the same amount of turn. Many simple machines give you that kind of trade: a smaller push used over a longer distance.
facts: The center of the nut is the center of the wrench’s turn.

entries.title: Why does a paper towel pull up water?
entries.answer: A paper towel is made of many small fibers with narrow spaces between them. Water sticks to the fibers and to other water molecules. When one edge of the paper touches a spill, water spreads into those spaces and pulls more water along with it. It can even climb up part of the towel. A smooth sheet of plastic does not have the same tiny pathways.
facts: A paper towel can get wet above the edge where it first touched the water.

entries.title: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster?
entries.answer: In an open pot, water boils when its bubbles can push against the air above it. A pressure cooker traps much of the steam under a tight lid. The trapped steam raises the pressure, so the water can get hotter before it boils. Food in the cooker is then surrounded by hotter water or steam than it could usually meet in an open pot.
facts: The same rule also helps explain why water often boils at a lower temperature high in the mountains.

entries.title: Why does a sliced apple turn brown?
entries.answer: A freshly cut apple has new surfaces where the fruit’s cells meet the air. An enzyme in those cells helps oxygen take part in changes that form brown-colored material. The changes can go faster on a damaged surface than inside a whole apple. Lemon juice can slow the browning for a while because it changes conditions at the wet surface. Browning does not turn the apple into toast. Those two changes look a little alike but happen in different ways.
facts: Crushing or cutting fruit can bring its cells into contact with more air.

entries.title: Why does a suction cup stick to a smooth window?
entries.answer: Pressing a suction cup flat against a smooth surface pushes out much of the air underneath it. When the cup tries to spring back, the tight edge keeps most air from flowing back in. The air outside now pushes harder than the thin air in the space under the cup. The difference in those pushes holds the cup against the window.
facts: If air leaks in along the edge, the cup can come loose without anyone pulling it.

entries.title: Why does a wool sweater help keep you warm?
entries.answer: Wool comes from the coat of an animal, often a sheep. Its fine fibers often have little bends or waves. When the fibers are made into yarn and fabric, they can trap small spaces filled with air. Air that stays mostly still can slow the movement of heat away from your body. That helps make a wool sweater feel warm when you put it on in cool weather. The fabric does not have to make extra heat of its own to be useful.
facts: Many wool fibers have a natural bend or wave called crimp.

entries.title: Why does plywood have layers that face different ways?
entries.answer: A piece of solid wood often splits more easily in the direction its fibers run. In plywood, a panel is made by gluing together thin sheets of wood. The grain of one sheet often runs across the grain of the next one. That can keep the whole panel from having one easy direction to split. It can also help the sheet stay flatter when moisture changes. Looking at a plywood edge may show several thin lines where the different sheets meet.
facts: A thin sheet of wood used as a layer is called veneer.

entries.title: Why does soda fizz when you open it?
entries.answer: A bottle of soda holds carbon dioxide mixed into the liquid. Inside the closed bottle, the gas above the drink pushes on the liquid. This higher pressure helps the liquid hold more dissolved gas. Opening the bottle lowers that pressure. Gas begins to leave the liquid, forming bubbles that rise and pop. Tiny rough places in a glass can give the bubbles places to start. When enough gas has escaped, the drink tastes flatter even though much of the liquid is still there.
facts: Carbon dioxide can remain dissolved in a drink even when you see very few bubbles.

entries.title: Why does twisting an ice tray make the cubes come out?
entries.answer: Water freezes inside the little pockets of an ice tray and takes their shape. In a flexible tray, a gentle twist changes the shape of those pockets a little. The solid cubes cannot bend to match the new shape the way the tray does. Some of their contact with the tray breaks, so the cubes can drop out when the tray is turned over.
facts: A soft-bottomed tray can also bend at the bottom of just one pocket to release a cube.

entries.title: Why does water from a faucet sometimes look white and bubbly?
entries.answer: Some faucet tips have a piece that brings small amounts of air into flowing water. Many tiny bubbles scatter light, so the stream can look pale or cloudy as it comes out. The bubbles can make the stream feel fuller even when the faucet is passing less water. The bubbles usually leave quickly when the water sits still in a glass.
facts: The part that mixes air into the flowing water is called an aerator.

entries.title: Why is there a curved pipe below many sinks?
entries.answer: A curved pipe below a sink can keep a little water after the rest of the water has drained. The water fills the low bend. Air from farther along the drain cannot easily get through this water, so the bent pipe helps keep drain smells away from the room. The next time water enters the sink, some pushes through and leaves fresh water in the bend.
facts: The curved part that holds this water is called a trap.
